user.title: Set up HEMS
user.description:
HEMS distributes your PV surplus automatically across hot water, home battery and flexible loads.

**How it works:** the meter at the grid connection reports whether you are currently exporting (surplus) or drawing power. From the PV forecast, storage level and your priorities, HEMS derives its recommendation and control.

This step only records the meter and the basic values. **You add your devices afterwards in the HEMS panel in the sidebar** — there they all sit on one page and can be changed, extended and removed at any time.

data_description.meter_entity: Sensor with the current power at the grid connection point in watts. Expected: positive = import, negative = export.
data_description.invert_meter: Enable if your meter reports export as a positive value.
data_description.pv_power_entity: Sensor with the current total PV production across all planes. Used for the load flow and to refine the recommendation.
data_description.invert_pv_power: Enable if your inverter reports PV power with a flipped sign (negative = production).
data_description.pv_minus_battery: Enable if PV and battery are measured at the same point (hybrid inverter), so the PV reading contains the battery power. HEMS then subtracts the battery power from the measured PV (discharge lowers it, charge raises it).
data_description.weather_entity: Weather entity whose daily forecast feeds the planning: on an overcast next day HEMS fully charges the battery instead of covering only the night.
data_description.baseline_load_w: Typical continuous consumption of the house during the day without large consumers (fridge, network, standby).
data_description.night_load_w: Initial value for night-time consumption. HEMS learns the real value automatically from meter statistics after a few days.
data_description.priority_mode: Where should surplus go first? "Automatic" fills the battery first when yield is scarce so the night is covered; with plenty of yield the EV may charge first. Hot-water base heating always has top priority.
data_description.free_capacity_kwh: The "Capacity free" binary sensor turns on when this much energy is available over the given duration without touching the reserve or the night coverage.
data_description.free_capacity_h: Duration over which the energy demand must be covered. PV surplus expected within this window counts towards the free capacity.

init.title: Configure HEMS
init.description: Add, edit or remove devices, and change base values and priorities. Every entry can be adjusted at any time.

add_forecast.title: PV forecast plane
add_forecast.description: A **PV forecast plane** provides the expected solar production, e.g. from the Forecast.Solar or Solcast integration. Add multiple planes (east/west roof) separately — HEMS sums them automatically.

data_description.name: A short label for this forecast plane, e.g. the roof orientation (used only for display).
data_description.energy_today: Sensor with the forecast total PV energy for today (kWh), from your forecast integration (e.g. Forecast.Solar, Solcast).
data_description.energy_remaining: Sensor with the forecast remaining PV energy for the rest of today (kWh). Feeds the live surplus and recommendation calculations.
data_description.energy_tomorrow: Sensor with the forecast total PV energy for tomorrow (kWh). Used to decide whether the battery should be charged fully today as a buffer against a poor day ahead.

add_storage.title: Storage
add_storage.description: A **storage** (home battery) buffers PV surplus for the night. HEMS derives a target state of charge from night consumption and reserve and schedules charging within the solar window.

data.name: Name
data.soc_set_entity: Target SoC entity (soc_set, device-side charge cap, optional)

data_description.charge_setpoint_entity: Number entity HEMS can use to set the current charging power.
data_description.discharge_setpoint_entity: Number entity HEMS can use to set the current discharge power (e.g. “discharge at 500 W now”).
data_description.reserve_soc: The battery should not be discharged below this level (emergency reserve).
data_description.max_charge_w: Charging power limit; determines how quickly the battery fills within the solar window.
data_description.max_discharge_w: Limit of the discharge power; the battery cannot deliver more than this to the house.
data_description.cold_reserve: This storage joins discharging only when the average SoC of the other storages drops below the reserve threshold (with hysteresis). It always participates in charging, proportionally to its free capacity.
data_description.name: A short label for this storage, e.g. its physical location or unit name.
data_description.soc_entity: Sensor with the current state of charge in percent.
data_description.power_entity: Sensor with the current charge/discharge power in watts. Convention: positive = discharging into the house, negative = charging. Used for the load-flow display and the auto-mode control loop.
data_description.mode_entity: Optional select/input_select HEMS toggles between charging and discharging direction (e.g. Zendure's ac_mode). Only needed if your storage requires a mode switch in addition to a setpoint.
data_description.mode_charge_option: The option value that puts the storage into charging mode. Must match one of the select's available options exactly (case-sensitive) — the config check flags it otherwise.
data_description.mode_discharge_option: The option value that puts the storage into discharging mode. Must match one of the select's available options exactly (case-sensitive) — the config check flags it otherwise.
data_description.soc_set_entity: Optional number entity that caps how far the storage charges on its own (device-side target SoC). Some storages ignore an input power limit of 0 and keep charging toward this target regardless — set it if that applies to yours.
data_description.capacity_kwh: Usable capacity of this storage; used to distribute charge/discharge power across multiple storages and for the SoC forecast.

add_thermal.title: Hot water storage
add_thermal.description: A **hot water storage** stores surplus as heat. The base target is always maintained — from the grid if necessary. Heating up to the comfort target happens only on PV surplus.

data.name: Name
data.boost_soc_on: PV boost: battery SoC to start (%)
data.boost_soc_off: PV boost: battery SoC to stop (%)
data.boost_saldo_on_w: PV boost: grid balance to start (W)
data.boost_saldo_off_w: PV boost: grid balance to stop (W)
data.control_entity: Control entity for auto mode (water_heater, or a switch)

data_description.base_target: This temperature is always maintained, from the grid if necessary.
data_description.comfort_target: Heating up to this temperature only happens on PV surplus.
data_description.block_start: Start of the daily period in which no hot water is prepared. Leave both empty for no blocking.
data_description.block_end: End of the blocked period. An end before the start means the window runs over midnight (e.g. 18:00 to 06:00).
data_description.legionella_weekday: Weekly hygiene window: on this day the target is raised to the legionella target regardless of surplus — from the grid if necessary. "Disabled" turns the feature off.
data_description.legionella_start: Local start time of the weekly legionella window.
data_description.legionella_end: End of the window. An end before the start runs over midnight.
data_description.legionella_target: Target temperature held during the legionella window.
data_description.boost_soc_on: Heating to the comfort target is only recommended once the total storage SoC reaches this level.
data_description.boost_soc_off: The boost recommendation ends when the SoC falls below this level (hysteresis).
data_description.boost_saldo_on_w: Grid balance that must be reached to start the boost; negative = export (e.g. -2800 = exporting 2.8 kW).
data_description.boost_saldo_off_w: Grid balance at which the boost ends (positive = import).
data_description.name: A short label for this hot-water system (used only for display).
data_description.temp_entity: Sensor with the current hot-water temperature. Without it, HEMS still recommends a target but cannot show or verify the actual temperature.
data_description.control_entity: Entity HEMS switches on/off in auto mode. A water_heater also carries the target temperature; a switch only turns it on/off — then set the target on the number below.
data_description.setpoint_entity: Number HEMS writes the target temperature to when the control entity is a switch (e.g. a Modbus heat pump exposing an enable switch and a target-temperature number separately). Leave empty for a water_heater.

add_switchable.title: Switchable load
add_switchable.description: **Switchable (sheddable) loads** are devices HEMS can only turn on or off — their power cannot be modulated. Examples: heat pump (SG-Ready/blocking contact), heating rod, pool pump. Minimum runtime and minimum pause protect the device from frequent cycling.

data_description.min_on_min: Once switched on, the device stays on for at least this long.
data_description.min_off_min: After switching off, the device stays off for at least this long.
data_description.max_block_min: The device is never blocked for longer than this per day.
data_description.priority: 1 = highest priority. When surplus is scarce, loads with higher priority are served first.
data_description.name: A short label for this load (used only for display, e.g. in the recommendation and load-flow card).
data_description.switch_entity: Switch (or climate) entity HEMS turns on and off based on surplus.
data_description.power_entity: Sensor with the current power draw in watts. HEMS learns the expected power from it while the load is running, used to decide whether surplus covers it.
data_description.mode_heat_option: Climate entities only: the HVAC mode that means "heating" (usually "heat", on some systems "auto"). HEMS sets it via set_hvac_mode rather than calling turn_on, which many integrations do not implement. Empty = "heat". If the appliance already runs in another mode, HEMS leaves it alone.

add_modulated.title: Modulated load
add_modulated.description: **Modulated loads** can adjust their power consumption continuously. The typical example is a wallbox whose charging current (in amperes) can be regulated between a minimum and maximum. HEMS continuously tracks the setpoint to the available surplus.

data_description.current_entity: Number entity used to set the current setpoint.
data_description.switch_entity: Optional switch HEMS can use to turn the device on and off entirely (e.g. wallbox charging enable).
data_description.min_on_min: Once started, the device runs for at least this long before HEMS stops it (e.g. charge the EV for at least 10 minutes).
data_description.min_a: The device cannot operate below this current (wallbox minimum is usually 6 A).
data_description.priority: 1 = highest priority. When surplus is scarce, loads with higher priority are served first.
data_description.name: A short label for this load (used only for display, e.g. the wallbox name).
data_description.power_entity: Sensor with the current power draw in watts. Used for the load-flow display and to learn the load's actual demand.
data_description.max_a: The device is never commanded above this current.
data_description.phases: Number of connected phases; used to convert between current (A) and power (W).
data_description.min_off_min: After HEMS stops the device, it stays off for at least this long before it can restart.

add_heating.title: Heating
add_heating.description:
A **heating system** (heat pump, heating rod) is a switchable load with weather compensation. It competes for the same surplus budget as any other load, but adds three things: **frost protection** forces it on once it gets cold outside — past surplus and minimum pause, from the grid if necessary. During the **lock months** and above the **heating limit** it never heats. If a flow setpoint entity is configured, HEMS writes it from the **heating curve**.

HEMS is not a safety device and does not replace the appliance's own frost protection.

data_description.name: A short label, used for display only.
data_description.switch_entity: How HEMS enables or blocks the appliance. A **switch** is typically the SG-Ready or utility blocking contact: HEMS then only blocks, and the appliance keeps its own control including frost protection. A **climate** entity really switches the heat generator off — there, the HEMS frost protection is the only fallback HEMS knows about.
data_description.mode_heat_option: Climate entities only: the HVAC mode that means "heating" (usually "heat", on some systems "auto"). HEMS sets it via set_hvac_mode rather than calling turn_on, which many integrations do not implement. Empty = "heat". If the appliance already runs in another mode, HEMS leaves it alone.
data_description.power_entity: HEMS learns the running power draw from it and then knows how much surplus the appliance needs. Without it, HEMS assumes a conservatively high flat value.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Drives frost protection, heating limit and heating curve. Without its own sensor HEMS uses the temperature of the globally configured weather entity. With neither, HEMS does not control at all: it neither switches the appliance on nor off, but leaves it alone.
data_description.flow_setpoint_entity: Number entity for the flow target temperature. Without it the heating curve is display only — HEMS then merely enables and blocks.
data_description.frost_on_c: Once the outdoor temperature falls to this value, switching on is forced — regardless of surplus, minimum pause and summer lock, from the grid if necessary. 0 does not disable frost protection; it puts the threshold at freezing point, which is tight because a heating circuit keeps cooling down after being switched off.
data_description.frost_off_c: Frost protection only ends above this value. The gap to the on threshold is the hysteresis — without it the appliance would cycle at the threshold.
data_description.heat_on_c: Below this outdoor temperature the house needs heat.
data_description.heat_off_c: Above this outdoor temperature heating stops (heating limit, with hysteresis against the on threshold). Between the two values the previous state stands.
data_description.curve_base_c: The flow setpoint at 0 °C outdoor temperature. The default suits underfloor heating; a radiator circuit needs considerably more.
data_description.curve_slope: By how many kelvin the flow rises per kelvin of outdoor cold. Flow = base point − outdoor temperature × slope.
data_description.vlt_min_c: The flow setpoint never falls below this value.
data_description.vlt_max_c: The flow setpoint never rises above this value.
data_description.heat_lock_from_month: First month of the summer lock (1 = January, inclusive). During the lock months heating is never recommended — only frost protection still applies. If the start month is greater than the end month, the lock runs across the turn of the year. 0 in either field = no lock.
data_description.heat_lock_to_month: Last month of the summer lock (inclusive).
data_description.min_on_min: Once on, the appliance stays on for at least this long.
data_description.min_off_min: After switching off, the appliance stays off for at least this long. Frost protection bypasses this.
data_description.max_block_min: Once the appliance has been off this long, it is switched on even without surplus. Measured from the entity's last state change, whoever caused it.
data_description.priority: 1 = most important. When surplus is scarce, the least important load gives way first. Heating systems and switchable loads share one ranking.

config_fehler.title: HEMS: configuration error ({anzahl})
config_fehler.description:
Auto mode would fail with the current configuration:
{fehler}
